name: pixelsort
role: Python pixel-sorting glitch effect for stills: interval functions, masks, angle, sort keys
notes: 2026-11-27: Triage: assess. g-mic, imagemagick and libvips have no pixel-sort operator; one effect for glitch transitions on stills or frame sequences. Lead details confirmed: PyPI 1.0.2 (2026-09-03), GitHub licence MIT, 877 stars, last push 2026-09-03.
2026-11-27: pixelsort 1.0.2 declares an unpinned Pillow requirement but imports PIL.PyAccess, which newer Pillow removed; a fresh install on Pillow 13 fails at import. The fixture pins Pillow 10.4.0.

2026-11-27: No seed option. The random and waves interval functions and the randomness option draw from Python's global random, so call random.seed(n) first when using the API; the CLI cannot be made repeatable that way, so use threshold, edges or a mask there.

evidence.result: Pass: 9 of 9 predeclared checks plus repeat-run equality. Threshold on a generated 240x135 image: 3646 spans, 0 unsorted by lightness, 0 rows not a permutation, 19913 pixels changed. Hue with interval none: 0 of 135 rows unsorted. Mask left right half untouched. Angle 90 sorted 240 of 240 columns. CLI equals API. Seeded random repeats across processes; CLI random differs between runs.
evidence.scope: Python venv, macOS arm64, 240x135 generated RGB still: threshold, none, mask, angle 90 and random intervals with lightness and hue keys; no edges, waves, file intervals, 4K speed or sequences

summary: Small Python module and CLI that sorts runs of pixels along rows (or columns via angle) by lightness, hue, saturation, intensity or minimum channel. Run boundaries come from brightness thresholds, edge detection, random or wave widths, or a black-and-white interval image, and a mask can protect regions. Writes ordinary images. Pure Python on Pillow, so slow at 4K; its strength is the one glitch effect no neighbour has.
use_when: Pixel-sort glitch stills or transitions that ImageMagick, G'MIC and libvips have no operator for
Threshold-bounded streaks sorted by hue or lightness, masked to part of the frame
Repeatable frames from the Python API with a seeded global random
avoid_when: Large frames or long sequences: pure Python, use libvips or G'MIC for speed
Repeatable random intervals from the CLI: it has no seed, use the API
Other glitch or filter looks: G'MIC has about a thousand filters

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install pixelsort==1.0.2 Pillow==10.4.0

assessment.rationale: MIT, 1.0.2 released 2026-09-03 with a push the same day. Fills a gap no neighbour covers. Breaks on current Pillow (PyAccess import), so a pin is needed; random intervals use the unseeded global random.
